scenes.heading: Understanding usage rights and licensing terms

sents.d: Understanding usage rights and licensing terms
Vague usage terms are the most common source of UGC pricing disputes.

Usage rights define where a brand can use your content and for how long — organic-only social posting, paid advertising, whitelisting (running ads through your own handle), or website/print use are all different tiers that should be priced differently.
Always put a specific time limit on usage rights (e.g. 6 months) rather than granting indefinite use, so a brand that wants to keep running your content longer has to come back and pay again.

If a brand's contract has vague or unlimited usage language, it's worth asking for clarification and adjusting your rate — content running in paid ads indefinitely is worth substantially more than a single organic post.

take: Time-limit usage rights and charge more for paid ads.
